# Dataset upload

## Components

### Spreadsheet loader

The spreadsheet-loader component asks the user to select a file from their
machine with a file dialog, which is then parsed to extract metadata, and
stored in OPFS (which is a virtual filesystem in the users's browser). All of
this happens on the client side, only the spreadsheet metadata is provided to
the server, and presented as the component's properties.

This component must be custom made since there is no pre-existing equivalent.
See [requirements](#requirements) for the reasoning behind using OPFS.

Children:
- upload button:
    - open file dialog to get file path
    - import file to OPFS and extract metadata
    - present metadata to server as properties

Properties:
- `opfs_path: str`
- `table_names: List[str]`
- `column_names: Dict[TableName, str]`

### Import dataset modal

This is the import screen (prev. known as the "upload screen"), which uses a
(dash bootstrap) modal to prevent the user from interacting with other parts of
the site until the dataset is imported or discarded. It has a
[spreadsheet-loader](#spreadsheet-loader) component to import files, and ok &
cancel buttons to proceed or discard.

Children:
- [spreadsheet loader](#spreadsheet-loader)
- ok button:
    - finalize import
    - hide modal
    - show [conf modal](dataset-conf.md#config-modal) (which in turn
      transitions the user to the datasets page)
- cancel button:
    - discard import
    - hide modal

## Implementation

See [requirements](#requirements) at the bottom for the reasons behind this
implementation.

### Stores

Boolean flags are used to toggle modal visibility. All modal-flags have type
`bool` and a callback to set its modal `is_open` property.

- datasets: list of [Dataset](#python-types)
- import-modal-flag
- conf-modal-flag

### Callbacks

**main-menu**:
- upload-button:
    - on_click: set import-modal-flag

**import-modal**:
- ok-button (disabled):
    - on_click(opfs_path, tables_names, column_names):
        - append dataset metadata to datasets
        - reset import-modal-flag
        - set conf-modal-flag
- cancel-button:
    - on_click(opfs_path):
        - call [delete_file(opfs_path)](#delete_file)
        - reset import-modal-flag

**spreadsheet-loader**:
- allowed={'csv', 'xlsx'}
- multiple=false
- upload-button:
    - on_click:
        - javascript:
            - call [import_file](#import_file) -> opfs_path
            - call [get_spreadsheet_metadata](#import_file)(opfs_path) -> metadata
        - python:
            - call [add_dataset](#add_dataset)(metadata)
            - enable parent ok button

### Javascript types

```typescript
type SpreadsheetMeta = {
    opfs_path: string
    table_names: string[]
    column_names: Map<TableName, string[]>
}
```

### Javascript functions

Javascript functions can either be called within a [clientside
callback](https://dash.plotly.com/clientside-callbacks), or be used in custom
components.

#### import_file

`function import_file(): string`

Imports a file from the users machine, stores it in OPFS, and returns the
internal file path.

1. select file via file dialog
2. load file from local machine
3. save in opfs
4. return opfs path

#### get_spreadsheet_metadata

`function get_spreadsheet_metadata(opfs_path): SpreadsheetMeta`

Extracts spreadsheet metadata from a spreadsheet file stored in OPFS.

1. read file from opfs
2. use excel/csv libraries to parse metadata
3. return metadata

#### delete_file

`function delete_file(opfs_path)`

Removes file from OPFS.

### Python types

```python
class Dataset:
    """dataset metadata"""
    opfs_path: str
    name: str
    odm_version: str
    tables: Dict[TableName, OdmTableName]
```

### Python functions

#### add_dataset

`def add_dataset(opfs_path, table_names, column_names) -> Dataset`

Returns a dataset (metadata) object from the metadata provided, including auto-detected
values for ODM version and table mapping.

auto-detects:
- file type from filename extension
- ODM version and table mapping from table/column names

### Requirements

#### Privacy

Datasets must not be persisted on the server for privacy reasons. This also has
the added benefit of not requiring server storage space. Datasets must,
however, be stored somewhere accessible to the application.

- problems:
    - obviously can't use server file system
    - can't use server /tmp since it may not be mounted in memory, and even
      if it is in memory it won't be persistent for the user if the server
      restarts
    - dash is stateless, so we can't use server-side application state, and it
      wouldn't persist through server restart anyway
    - we don't want to use some complex server storage solution, so
      server-side db is out of the question
    - dcc.Store is client side (!), which that may be a good thing, however:
        - dcc.Store(memory/session) is not persistent
        - dcc.Store(local) can only hold 5-10 MB
    - can't use client filesystem since it requires to ask the user to pick the
      file every time (with the file dialog)
- solution:
    - use [OPFS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/File_System_Access_API#origin_private_file_system).
      The user will only be asked once to pick the file, after which it will be
      stored in the browser's OPFS for future access.
    - examples:
        - https://stackoverflow.com/a/71581910
        - https://webkit.org/blog/12257/the-file-system-access-api-with-origin-private-file-system/
    - only store metadata about the datasets in localStorage (if at all needed)
    - access dataset from client (to server) on demand (during validation)
